method.description: Lexical/rendering divergence indicator; not a doctrinal truth score or majority vote.
method.normalization: case, punctuation, footnote markers, and common KJV archaisms normalized
method.public_ranking_guard: minimum 8 POB tokens and three length-compatible references
method.public_headline: POB novelty × square-root(reference consensus); documented risk is excluded

sources.bsb: Berean Standard Bible (Public Domain / CC0). bereanbible.com.
sources.asv: American Standard Version (1901; Public Domain). ebible.org/asv/.
sources.brenton: Brenton's translation of the Septuagint (1844/1851; Public Domain). ebible.org/eng-Brenton/.
sources.kjv: King James Version, ebible.org 2006 transcription (Public Domain in US).

pob.text: The oracle that Habakkuk the prophet saw:[a]

spob.text: The prophetic message that Habakkuk the prophet saw:[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: This is the burden that Habakkuk the prophet received in a vision:
public_domain_references.web: The revelation which Habakkuk the prophet saw.
public_domain_references.asv: The burden which Habakkuk the prophet did see.
public_domain_references.kjv: The burden which Habakkuk the prophet did see.
public_domain_references.brenton: The burden which the prophet Ambacum saw.

pob.text: How long, O LORD, have I cried for help and you do not hear? I cry out to you, “Violence!” and you do not save.

spob.text: LORD, how long have I been crying for help without you hearing me? I shout to you, “Violence!” but you do not save.

public_domain_references.bsb: How long, O LORD, must I call for help but You do not hear, or cry out to You, “Violence!” but You do not save?
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh, how long will I cry, and you will not hear? I cry out to you “Violence!” and will you not save?
public_domain_references.asv: O Jehovah, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear? I cry out unto thee of violence, and thou wilt not save.
public_domain_references.kjv: O LORD, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear! [even] cry out unto thee [of] violence, and thou wilt not save!
public_domain_references.brenton: How long, O Lord, shall I cry out, and thou wilt not hearken? [how long] shall I cry out to thee being injured, and thou wilt not save?

pob.text: Why do you make me see wrongdoing[a], and why do you look at trouble? Destruction and violence are before me; strife comes to be[c][b], and contention rises up.

spob.text: Why do you make me see wrongdoing? Why do you look at trouble? Destruction[a] and violence are right in front of me. Strife begins, and conflict rises up.

public_domain_references.bsb: Why do You make me see iniquity? Why do You tolerate wrongdoing? Destruction and violence are before me. Strife is ongoing, and conflict abounds.
public_domain_references.web: Why do you show me iniquity, and look at perversity? For destruction and violence are before me. There is strife, and contention rises up.
public_domain_references.asv: Why dost thou show me iniquity, and look upon perverseness? for destruction and violence are before me; and there is strife, and contention riseth up.
public_domain_references.kjv: Why dost thou shew me iniquity, and cause [me] to behold grievance? for spoiling and violence [are] before me: and there are [that] raise up strife and contention.
public_domain_references.brenton: Wherefore hast thou shewn me troubles and griefs to look upon, misery and ungodliness? judgment is before me, and the judge receives a reward.

pob.text: Therefore the law grows numb, and justice never goes forth. For the wicked surrounds the righteous; therefore justice goes forth twisted.

spob.text: So the law becomes powerless, and justice is never carried out. The wicked close in around the righteous, so justice is carried out in a twisted way.

public_domain_references.bsb: Therefore the law is paralyzed, and justice never goes forth. For the wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.
public_domain_references.web: Therefore the law is paralyzed, and justice never prevails; for the wicked surround the righteous; therefore justice comes out perverted.
public_domain_references.asv: Therefore the law is slacked, and justice doth never go forth; for the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore justice goeth forth perverted.
public_domain_references.kjv: Therefore the law is slacked, and judgment doth never go forth: for the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore wrong judgment proceedeth.
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore the law is frustrated, and judgment proceeds not effectually, for the ungodly [man] prevails over the just; therefore perverse judgment will proceed.

pob.text: Look among the nations and see[a]; be astonished, be astounded[b]. For I am doing a work in your days that you would not believe if it were told.

spob.text: Look among the nations[a] and pay close attention. Be astonished—be utterly amazed! In your lifetime, I am doing a work[b] that you would not believe even if someone told you about it.

public_domain_references.bsb: “Look at the nations and observe— be utterly astounded! For I am doing a work in your days that you would never believe even if someone told you.
public_domain_references.web: “Look among the nations, watch, and wonder marvelously; for I am working a work in your days which you will not believe though it is told you.
public_domain_references.asv: Behold ye among the nations, and look, and wonder marvellously; for I am working a work in your days, which ye will not believe though it be told you.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Behold ye among the heathen, and regard, and wonder marvellously: for [I] will work a work in your days, [which] ye will not believe, though it be told [you].
public_domain_references.brenton: Behold, ye despisers, and look, and wonder marvellously, and vanish: for I work a work in your days, which ye will in no wise believe, though a man declare [it to you].

pob.text: For behold[a], I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation[b], which marches through the broad places of the earth to seize dwelling places not its own.

spob.text: For look, I am raising up the Chaldeans,[a] a harsh and reckless nation.[b] They march across the wide regions of the earth, seizing homes that belong to other people.

public_domain_references.bsb: For behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans — that ruthless and impetuous nation which marches through the breadth of the earth to seize dwellings not their own.
public_domain_references.web: For, behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation who march through the width of the earth, to possess dwelling places that are not theirs.
public_domain_references.asv: For, lo, I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, that march through the breadth of the earth, to possess dwelling-places that are not theirs.
public_domain_references.kjv: For, lo, I raise up the Chaldeans, [that] bitter and hasty nation, which shall march through the breadth of the land, to possess the dwellingplaces [that are] not theirs.
public_domain_references.brenton: Wherefore, behold, I stir up the Chaldeans, the bitter and hasty nation, that walks upon the breadth of the earth, to inherit tabernacles not his own.

pob.text: It is dreadful and fearsome[b][a]; its justice and its majesty proceed from itself.

spob.text: This nation is dreadful and terrifying. Its standards of justice and its claims to honor come from itself, not from any higher authority.

public_domain_references.bsb: They are dreaded and feared; from themselves they derive justice and sovereignty.
public_domain_references.web: They are feared and dreaded. Their judgment and their dignity proceed from themselves.
public_domain_references.asv: They are terrible and dreadful; their judgment and their dignity proceed from themselves.
public_domain_references.kjv: They [are] terrible and dreadful: their judgment and their dignity shall proceed of themselves.
public_domain_references.brenton: He is terrible and famous; his judgment shall proceed of himself, and his dignity shall come out of himself.

pob.text: His horses are swifter than leopards and fiercer than wolves at dusk[a]. His horsemen spread out; his horsemen come from far away. They fly like an eagle hurrying to devour.

spob.text: His horses are faster than leopards and fiercer than wolves at dusk. His horsemen spread out. They come from far away, flying like an eagle[a] rushing to devour.

public_domain_references.bsb: Their horses are swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves of the night. Their horsemen charge ahead, and their cavalry comes from afar. They fly like a vulture, swooping down to devour.
public_domain_references.web: Their horses also are swifter than leopards, and are more fierce than the evening wolves. Their horsemen press proudly on. Yes, their horsemen come from afar. They fly as an eagle that hurries to devour.
public_domain_references.asv: Their horses also are swifter than leopards, and are more fierce than the evening wolves; and their horsemen press proudly on: yea, their horsemen come from far; they fly as an eagle that hasteth to devour.
public_domain_references.kjv: Their horses also are swifter than the leopards, and are more fierce than the evening wolves: and their horsemen shall spread themselves, and their horsemen shall come from far; they shall fly as the eagle [that] hasteth to eat.
public_domain_references.brenton: And his horses shall bound [more swiftly] than leopards, and [they are] fiercer than the wolves of Arabia: and his horsemen shall ride forth, and shall rush from far; and they shall fly as an eagle hasting to eat.

pob.text: All of them come for violence[a]; the set of their faces is forward[c][b], and they gather captives like sand.

spob.text: They all come to commit violence. Their faces are fixed straight ahead,[a] and they gather captives as countless as sand.

public_domain_references.bsb: All of them come bent on violence; their hordes advance like the east wind; they gather prisoners like sand.
public_domain_references.web: All of them come for violence. Their hordes face forward. They gather prisoners like sand.
public_domain_references.asv: They come all of them for violence; the set of their faces is forwards; and they gather captives as the sand.
public_domain_references.kjv: They shall come all for violence: their faces shall sup up [as] the east wind, and they shall gather the captivity as the sand.
public_domain_references.brenton: Destruction shall come upon ungodly men, resisting with their adverse front, and he shall gather the captivity as the sand.

pob.text: He mocks kings[a], and rulers are a laughingstock to him. He laughs at every fortress; he heaps up earth and captures it.

spob.text: He scorns kings and treats rulers as laughable. He laughs at every fortress, piles earth against it to make a siege ramp, and captures it.

public_domain_references.bsb: They scoff at kings and make rulers an object of scorn. They laugh at every fortress and build up siege ramps to seize it.
public_domain_references.web: Yes, they scoff at kings, and princes are a derision to them. They laugh at every stronghold, for they build up an earthen ramp and take it.
public_domain_references.asv: Yea, he scoffeth at kings, and princes are a derision unto him; he derideth every stronghold; for he heapeth up dust, and taketh it.
public_domain_references.kjv: And they shall scoff at the kings, and the princes shall be a scorn unto them: they shall deride every strong hold; for they shall heap dust, and take it.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he shall be at his ease with kings, and princes are his toys, and he shall mock at every strong-hold, and shall cast a mound, and take possession of it.

pob.text: Then he sweeps by like the wind and passes on—he becomes guilty[b][a]; this strength of his is his god.

spob.text: Then he rushes past like the wind[b] and moves on. He becomes guilty: he treats his own strength as his god.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Then they sweep by like the wind and pass on through. They are guilty; their own strength is their god.”
public_domain_references.web: Then they sweep by like the wind and go on. They are indeed guilty, whose strength is their god.”
public_domain_references.asv: Then shall he sweep by [as] a wind, and shall pass over, and be guilty, [even] he whose might is his god.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then shall [his] mind change, and he shall pass over, and offend, [imputing] this his power unto his god.
public_domain_references.brenton: Then shall he change his spirit, and he shall pass through, and make an atonement, [saying], This strength [belongs] to my god.

pob.text: Are you not from of old, O Yahweh my God, my Holy One? We will not die.[a] O Yahweh, you have appointed him for judgment, and you, O Rock, have established him for reproof.

spob.text: Have you not existed since ancient times, Yahweh my God, my Holy One? We will not die.[a] Yahweh, you appointed him to carry out judgment. Rock, you established him to bring correction.

public_domain_references.bsb: Are You not from everlasting, O LORD, my God, my Holy One? We will not die. O LORD, You have appointed them to execute judgment; O Rock, You have established them for correction.
public_domain_references.web: Aren’t you from everlasting, Yahweh my God, my Holy One? We will not die. Yahweh, you have appointed them for judgment. You, Rock, have established him to punish.
public_domain_references.asv: Art not thou from everlasting, O Jehovah my God, my Holy One? we shall not die. O Jehovah, thou hast ordained him for judgment; and thou, O Rock, hast established him for correction.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ [Art] thou not from everlasting, O LORD my God, mine Holy One? we shall not die. O LORD, thou hast ordained them for judgment; and, O mighty God, thou hast established them for correction.
public_domain_references.brenton: [Art] not thou from the beginning, O Lord God, my Holy One? and surely we shall not die. O Lord, thou hast established it for judgment, and he has formed me to chasten [with] his correction.

pob.text: Your eyes are too pure to look on evil[a], and you cannot gaze at wrongdoing[c][b]. Why then do you look on the treacherous and keep silent when the wicked swallows up one more righteous than he?

spob.text: Your eyes are too pure to watch evil, and you cannot look at wrongdoing. Why, then, do you watch those who act treacherously? Why do you remain silent when a wicked person swallows up someone more righteous than he is?

public_domain_references.bsb: Your eyes are too pure to look upon evil, and You cannot tolerate wrongdoing. So why do You tolerate the faithless? Why are You silent while the wicked swallow up those more righteous than themselves?
public_domain_references.web: You who have purer eyes than to see evil, and who cannot look on perversity, why do you tolerate those who deal treacherously and keep silent when the wicked swallows up the man who is more righteous than he,
public_domain_references.asv: Thou that art of purer eyes than to behold evil, and that canst not look on perverseness, wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal treacherously, and holdest thy peace when the wicked swalloweth up the man that is more righteous than he;
public_domain_references.kjv: [Thou art] of purer eyes than to behold evil, and canst not look on iniquity: wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal treacherously, [and] holdest thy tongue when the wicked devoureth [the man that is] more righteous than he?
public_domain_references.brenton: [His] eye is too pure to behold evil [doings], and to look upon grievous afflictions: wherefore dost thou look upon despisers? wilt thou be silent when the ungodly swallows up the just?

pob.text: You make man like the fish of the sea[a], like creeping things that have no ruler over them.

spob.text: You make man[a] like fish in the sea, like crawling creatures with no ruler over them.

public_domain_references.bsb: You have made men like the fish of the sea, like creeping things that have no ruler.
public_domain_references.web: and make men like the fish of the sea, like the creeping things that have no ruler over them?
public_domain_references.asv: and makest men as the fishes of the sea, as the creeping things, that have no ruler over them?
public_domain_references.kjv: And makest men as the fishes of the sea, as the creeping things, [that have] no ruler over them?
public_domain_references.brenton: And wilt thou make men as the fishes of the sea, and as the reptiles which have no guide?

pob.text: He brings all of them up with a hook[a]; he drags him away with his net, and gathers him in with his dragnet[b]. Therefore he rejoices and exults.

spob.text: He pulls all of them up with a hook. He drags one of them away with his net and gathers him in with his dragnet.[a] So he rejoices and celebrates.

public_domain_references.bsb: The foe pulls all of them up with a hook; he catches them in his dragnet, and gathers them in his fishing net; so he rejoices gladly.
public_domain_references.web: He takes up all of them with the hook. He catches them in his net and gathers them in his dragnet. Therefore he rejoices and is glad.
public_domain_references.asv: He taketh up all of them with the angle, he catcheth them in his net, and gathereth them in his drag: therefore he rejoiceth and is glad.
public_domain_references.kjv: They take up all of them with the angle, they catch them in their net, and gather them in their drag: therefore they rejoice and are glad.
public_domain_references.brenton: He has brought up destruction with a hook, and drawn one with a casting net, and caught another in his drags: therefore shall his heart rejoice and be glad.

pob.text: Therefore he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet[a], because by them his portion is rich and his food is plentiful.

spob.text: So he worships his net by offering sacrifices to it, and he burns incense to his dragnet. He does this because they give him a rich share and plenty of food.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Therefore he sacrifices to his dragnet and burns incense to his fishing net, for by these things his portion is sumptuous and his food is rich.
public_domain_references.web: Therefore he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet, because by them his life is luxurious and his food is good.
public_domain_references.asv: Therefore he sacrificeth unto his net, and burneth incense unto his drag; because by them his portion is fat, and his food plenteous.
public_domain_references.kjv: Therefore they sacrifice unto their net, and burn incense unto their drag; because by them their portion [is] fat, and their meat plenteous.
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore will he sacrifice to his drag, and burn incense to his casting-net, because by them he has made his portion fat, and his meats choice.

pob.text: Will he therefore keep emptying his net and continually slaughtering nations without mercy?[a][b]

spob.text: So will he keep emptying his net and slaughtering nations again and again without mercy?

public_domain_references.bsb: Will he, therefore, empty his net and continue to slay nations without mercy?
public_domain_references.web: Will he therefore continually empty his net, and kill the nations without mercy?
public_domain_references.asv: Shall he therefore empty his net, and spare not to slay the nations continually?
public_domain_references.kjv: Shall they therefore empty their net, and not spare continually to slay the nations?
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore will he cast his net, and will not spare to slay the nations continually.

pob.text: I will stand at my guard post and station myself on the rampart[a]; I will keep watch to see what he will speak in me[b], and what I should answer concerning my complaint.

spob.text: I will stand at my guard post and take my place on the fortified wall. I will keep watch to learn what he will say to me[a] and what answer I should give about my complaint.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: I will stand at my guard post and station myself on the ramparts. I will watch to see what He will say to me, and how I should answer when corrected.
public_domain_references.web: I will stand at my watch and set myself on the ramparts, and will look out to see what he will say to me, and what I will answer concerning my complaint.
public_domain_references.asv: I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will look forth to see what he will speak with me, and what I shall answer concerning my complaint.
public_domain_references.kjv: I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will watch to see what he will say unto me, and what I shall answer when I am reproved.
public_domain_references.brenton: I will stand upon my watch, and mount upon the rock, and watch to see what he will say by me, and what I shall answer when I am reproved.

pob.text: Then Yahweh answered me and said: “Write the vision; make it plain on tablets[a], so that one who reads it may run.”

spob.text: Then Yahweh replied to me: “Write the vision on tablets, and make it clear, so that whoever reads it may run.”[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Then the LORD answered me: “Write down this vision and clearly inscribe it on tablets, so that a herald may run with it.
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh answered me, “Write the vision, and make it plain on tablets, that he who runs may read it.
public_domain_references.asv: And Jehovah answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tablets, that he may run that readeth it.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make [it] plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the Lord answered me and said, Write the vision, and [that] plainly on a tablet, that he that reads it may run.

pob.text: For the vision is still for the appointed time[a]; it hastens toward the end and will not lie. If it delays, wait for it, for it will surely come[b]; it will not be late.

spob.text: The vision will be fulfilled at the appointed time. It rushes toward its fulfillment[a] and will not prove false. If it delays, wait for it.[b] It will certainly come; it will not be late.

public_domain_references.bsb: For the vision awaits an appointed time; it testifies of the end and does not lie. Though it lingers, wait for it, since it will surely come and will not delay.
public_domain_references.web: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it, because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
public_domain_references.asv: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hasteth toward the end, and shall not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not delay.
public_domain_references.kjv: For the vision [is] yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the vision [is] yet for a time, and it shall shoot forth at the end, and not in vain: though he should tarry, wait for him; for he will surely come, and will not tarry.

pob.text: Look: his soul is puffed up; it is not upright within him, but the righteous will live by his faithfulness.

spob.text: Look! He is swollen with pride; deep inside, he is not upright. But the righteous person will live by his faithfulness.

public_domain_references.bsb: Look at the proud one; his soul is not upright — but the righteous will live by faith —
public_domain_references.web: Behold, his soul is puffed up. It is not upright in him, but the righteous will live by his faith.
public_domain_references.asv: Behold, his soul is puffed up, it is not upright in him; but the righteous shall live by his faith.
public_domain_references.kjv: Behold, his soul [which] is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith.
public_domain_references.brenton: If he should draw back, my soul has no pleasure in him: but the just shall live by my faith.

pob.text: Moreover[a], wine betrays; an arrogant man does not remain at rest. He enlarges his appetite like Sheol, and he is like death and is never satisfied[c][b]. He gathers to himself all the nations and collects to himself all the peoples.

spob.text: Moreover, wine betrays.[a] The arrogant man does not stay at rest.[b] He makes his appetite as wide as Sheol, the realm of the dead. Like death, he is never satisfied. He gathers all the nations for himself and collects all the peoples for himself.

public_domain_references.bsb: and wealth indeed betrays him. He is an arrogant man never at rest. He enlarges his appetite like Sheol, and like Death, he is never satisfied. He gathers all the nations to himself and collects all the peoples as his own.
public_domain_references.web: Yes, moreover, wine is treacherous: an arrogant man who doesn’t stay at home, who enlarges his desire as Sheol; he is like death and can’t be satisfied, but gathers to himself all nations and heaps to himself all peoples.
public_domain_references.asv: Yea, moreover, wine is treacherous, a haughty man, that keepeth not at home; who enlargeth his desire as Sheol, and he is as death, and cannot be satisfied, but gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all peoples.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Yea also, because he transgresseth by wine, [he is] a proud man, neither keepeth at home, who enlargeth his desire as hell, and [is] as death, and cannot be satisfied, but gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all people:
public_domain_references.brenton: But the arrogant man and the scorner, the boastful man, shall not finish anything; who has enlarged his desire as the grave, and like death he is never satisfied, and he will gather to himself all the nations, and will receive to himself all the peoples.

pob.text: Will not all of these take up a taunt against him[a], with mockery and riddles about him, and say, “Woe to him who heaps up what is not his—how long?—and loads himself with pledged goods!”

spob.text: Won’t all of them mock him with taunts and riddles? They will say, “Woe to the one who piles up what belongs to others—how long can this go on?—and weighs himself down with goods taken as security for debts!”[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Will not all of these take up a taunt against him, speaking with mockery and derision: ‘Woe to him who amasses what is not his and makes himself rich with many loans! How long will this go on?’
public_domain_references.web: Won’t all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, ‘Woe to him who increases that which is not his, and who enriches himself by extortion! How long?’
public_domain_references.asv: Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long? and that ladeth himself with pledges!
public_domain_references.kjv: Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth [that which is] not his! how long? and to him that ladeth himself with thick clay!
public_domain_references.brenton: Shall not all these take up a parable against him? and a proverb to tell against him? and they shall say, Woe to him that multiplies to himself the possessions which are not his! how long? and who heavily loads his yoke.

pob.text: Will not your creditors suddenly rise[a], and those who make you tremble awake? Then you will become plunder for them.

spob.text: Won’t the people you owe[a] suddenly rise up? Won’t those who make you tremble wake up? Then they will take you as plunder.

public_domain_references.bsb: Will not your creditors suddenly arise and those who disturb you awaken? Then you will become their prey.
public_domain_references.web: Won’t your debtors rise up suddenly, and wake up those who make you tremble, and you will be their victim?
public_domain_references.asv: Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee, and awake that shall vex thee, and thou shalt be for booty unto them?
public_domain_references.kjv: Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee, and awake that shall vex thee, and thou shalt be for booties unto them?
public_domain_references.brenton: For suddenly there shall arise up those that bite him, and they that plot against thee shall awake, and thou shalt be a plunder to them.

pob.text: Because you have plundered many nations[a], all the remnant of the peoples will plunder you—because of human blood and violence done to the land, to the city, and to all who dwell in it.

spob.text: You plundered many nations, so all the peoples who remain will plunder you. This is because you shed human blood and committed violence against the land, the city, and everyone who lives there.

public_domain_references.bsb: Because you have plundered many nations, the remnant of the people will plunder you— because of your bloodshed against man and your violence against the land, the city, and all their dwellers.
public_domain_references.web: Because you have plundered many nations, all the remnant of the peoples will plunder you because of men’s blood, and for the violence done to the land, to the city and to all who dwell in it.
public_domain_references.asv: Because thou hast plundered many nations, all the remnant of the peoples shall plunder thee, because of men’s blood, and for the violence done to the land, to the city and to all that dwell therein.
public_domain_references.kjv: Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee; because of men’s blood, and [for] the violence of the land, of the city, and of all that dwell therein.
public_domain_references.brenton: Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the nations that are left shall spoil [thee], because of the blood of men, and the sins of the land and city, and of all that dwell in it.

pob.text: Woe to him who gains evil profit for his house, to set his nest on high, to escape from the grasp of harm.

spob.text: I heard, and deep inside I trembled. At the sound, my lips quivered. Rot enters my bones, and I tremble where I stand. I wait quietly[a] for the day of distress, when the people who will invade us come against us.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: I heard and trembled within; my lips quivered at the sound. Decay entered my bones; I trembled where I stood. Yet I must wait patiently for the day of distress to come upon the people who invade us.
public_domain_references.web: I heard, and my body trembled. My lips quivered at the voice. Rottenness enters into my bones, and I tremble in my place because I must wait quietly for the day of trouble, for the coming up of the people who invade us.
public_domain_references.asv: I heard, and my body trembled, My lips quivered at the voice; Rottenness entereth into my bones, and I tremble in my place; Because I must wait quietly for the day of trouble, For the coming up of the people that invadeth us.
public_domain_references.kjv: When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself, that I might rest in the day of trouble: when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.
public_domain_references.brenton: I watched, and my belly trembled at the sound of the prayer of my lips, and trembling entered into my bones, and my frame was troubled within me; I will rest in the day of affliction, from going up to the people of my sojourning.

pob.text: Though the fig tree does not blossom[a], and there is no produce on the vines; the yield of the olive fails, and the fields produce no food; the flock is cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls[b],

spob.text: Though the fig tree does not bloom[a] and the vines bear no fruit, though the olive crop fails and the fields grow no food, though the flock is gone from its pen and there are no cattle in the stalls,

public_domain_references.bsb: Though the fig tree does not bud and no fruit is on the vines, though the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food, though the sheep are cut off from the fold and no cattle are in the stalls,
public_domain_references.web: For even though the fig tree doesn’t flourish, nor fruit be in the vines, the labor of the olive fails, the fields yield no food, the flocks are cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls,
public_domain_references.asv: For though the fig-tree shall not flourish, Neither shall fruit be in the vines; The labor of the olive shall fail, And the fields shall yield no food; The flock shall be cut off from the fold, And there shall be no herd in the stalls:
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither [shall] fruit [be] in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat; the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and [there shall be] no herd in the stalls:
public_domain_references.brenton: For [though] the fig-tree shall bear no fruit, and there shall be no produce on the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall produce no food: the sheep have failed from the pasture, and there are no oxen at the cribs;

pob.text: Yet I will rejoice in Yahweh[b][a]; I will exult in the God of my salvation.

spob.text: Yet I will rejoice in Yahweh. I will rejoice greatly in the God of my salvation.

public_domain_references.bsb: yet I will exult in the LORD; I will rejoice in the God of my salvation!
public_domain_references.web: yet I will rejoice in Yahweh. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!
public_domain_references.asv: Yet I will rejoice in Jehovah, I will joy in the God of my salvation.
public_domain_references.kjv: Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation.
public_domain_references.brenton: yet I will exult in the Lord, I will joy in God my Saviour.

pob.text:
The LORD, my Lord, is my strength; he makes my feet like the deer’s, and he causes me to tread on my heights.

For the choir director: with my stringed instruments.

spob.text:
The LORD, my Lord, is my strength. He makes my feet as sure-footed as a deer’s feet and enables me to walk on my high places.

For the choir director, with my stringed instruments.

public_domain_references.bsb: GOD the Lord is my strength; He makes my feet like those of a deer; He makes me walk upon the heights! For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments.
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh, the Lord, is my strength. He makes my feet like deer’s feet, and enables me to go in high places. For the music director, on my stringed instruments.
public_domain_references.asv: Jehovah, the Lord, is my strength; And he maketh my feet like hinds’ [feet], And will make me to walk upon my high places. For the Chief Musician, on my stringed instruments.
public_domain_references.kjv: The LORD God [is] my strength, and he will make my feet like hinds’ [feet], and he will make me to walk upon mine high places. To the chief singer on my stringed instruments.
public_domain_references.brenton: The Lord God is my strength, and he will perfectly strengthen my feet; he mounts me upon high places, that I may conquer by his song.
